paragraphs: (A Tanna of a baraita.) He is mentioned in [Yoma 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.18a.16) and [Tosefta Zavim, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Zavim.2.3), where he gives a teaching in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira. In [[Jerusalem Talmud] Sotah 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.1.2.7) he is mentioned in the dispute over the measure of seclusion, after Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira; but in the Babylonian [Sotah 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.4a.3) the reading there is Rabbi Elazar ben Yirmeyah. He is also mentioned in the work abbreviated בכ״ר, end of chapter 37.[^3]

notes.text: The supplied בכ״ר at the end of chapter 37 remains literal. The matching Bereshit Rabbah 37:8 witness is an explicit comparison, not proof of a printed correction history.
The consulted Yoma passage names Elazar ben Pinchas reporting Yehudah ben Beteira. Sotah has Elazar ben Yirmeyah. The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 37:8 also names Elazar ben Pinchas.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=547&lang=en) also lists Yoma and the Yerushalmi. Yoma names Elazar ben Pinchas, while the linked Tosefta abbreviates his given name ר״א. The Yerushalmi assigns the weaver’s thread comparison to ben Pinchas, and the Bavli to ben Yirmeyah. [Bereshit Rabbah 37:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.37.8) also names Elazar ben Pinchas. Hyman’s abbreviation בכ״ר remains in the text.
